items.title: Professor Longhair (Henry Roeland Byrd) Interview, 1975-11-13
items.q: I was working with the Midriffs. Who was in that band? That was George Miller.

ctx.x: So what band were you working with at this time? You had a band named the Midriffs, didn't you? It wasn't none of my band.

I was working with the Midriffs. Who was in that band? That was George Miller. He just recently died. He had three or four months ago. Maybe five. And Boots Alexis. Now what did he play? Oh, Boots? Yeah. He played the drums. And George Wilson, what did he play? He played an upright bass and he sung. Who else was in that band? They had Ellick Burrell. Ellick Burrell. Playing piano. He's now Duke Burrell. Duke Burrell. Yeah, he's in L.A. He changed his name. Yeah. No more Ellick. He's Duke Burrell now. And who else?
And you played piano? Well, after I joined the group.

items.title: Professor Longhair (Henry Roeland Byrd) Interview, 1969-05-30
items.q: And then we had this group, we called them Mid Drifts at that time. The Mid Drifts? Yeah. Uh, bass player was named George Miller.

ctx.x: Yeah. Yeah. Pappoos. His father helped me a lot when I was a kid. So I grabbed him and started training him. Once they could play an instrument, as much as I knew about music and the way I felt about it, I felt like I could help them. Uh huh. Not around reading. Yeah. I mean by air. Yeah. He was really a great little guitar player. You had to go and find him. Wherever you go, reason or what's not. They had to be real good at talking. Because his daddy was tremendous. Yeah. He helped me along with it. And then we…

I used to see you play when I was a kid. Yeah. When I was really young. Yeah. I can remember that group. Yeah. And myself. Yeah. You played fine piano I think. Yeah. I mean I just, I like to dream you know. Yeah. Yeah.
